- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price is falling sharply.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model may lag in adjusting; anticipate reversal and slightly increase forecast mid-period.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- In 30-day horizon, model often misses bottoming or toping; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, use 14-day moving average as anchor for final 10–15 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” (neutral), model tends to drift; apply smoothing or use 7-day average to dampen noise.
